ence speeds up to 7.69 FPS, approximately 38 times faster               domains such as indoor robotic visual navigation[42], vir-
than SOTA methods. The code is available at https:                      tual reality (VR)[44], and augmented reality (AR)[7].

    We design the Open-Vocabulary Multi-Source Spatial
Annotation and Reasoning Chain Generator (MSAG-RC) to                   2. Related Work
extract RGB images and depth information, enabling effec-               3D Visual Grounding. Most current 3DVG research[13,
tive transformation from 2D imagery to 3D spatial annota-               18, 27, 28, 43, 46, 55] follows supervised paradigms, requir-
tions. MSAG-RC uses open-vocabulary 2D detectors (e.g.,                 ing large-scale manual 3D labels from densely annotated
Grounding DINO [20]) and segmentation models such as                    datasets such as ScanRefer[4] and ReferIt3D[2], which
SAM2 [29] to obtain object masks and categories. By com-                align language descriptions with target objects in 3D scenes.
bining these with depth maps and camera parameters, the                    Representative works[5, 6, 10] address challenges in-
2D segmentation results are back-projected into 3D space                cluding text–point cloud alignment[33, 45], geometric fea-
to recover object-scale information. The projected 3D data              ture extraction[39, 40], and contextual cue modeling[57],
is encoded and fed into a VLM via prompt engineering to                 using approaches such as Transformer-based attention[11,
generate spatial pseudo-labels and reasoning chains, which              57, 58], contrastive learning[1], graph-based relational
serve as supervision to address the absence of spatial anno-            modeling[9, 13, 36, 50], and text-guided voxel pruning[10],
tations and reasoning guidance in zero-shot training.                   generally improving accuracy via manual 3D label supervi-
    To transfer reasoning knowledge and logical structures              sion. Weak supervision was also explored[54, 56], but not
within the chains to a compact model, we employ Reason-                 in 3D visual grounding.
ing Chain Distillation (RCD). A large teacher network ex-                  However, reliance on manual annotation limits general-
tracts such knowledge from the generated chains and dis-                ization to unseen environments. To address this, we propose
tills it into a lightweight student network. Due to the multi-          a zero-shot open-vocabulary 3DVG paradigm that uses au-
relational complexity of the chains, mapping target infor-              tomatically generated 3D pseudo labels to enhance adapt-
mation to sparse point clouds remains challenging. To mit-              ability and robustness in diverse 3D scenes.
igate this, we propose the Geometry-Aware Spatial Mod-                  Zero-Shot Open-Vocabulary 3DVG. Advances in large
eling (GeoSM) module, which encodes global context and                  language models (LLMs) [25] and vision–language mod-
local geometric relationships. GeoSM processes aligned vi-              els (VLMs) [12, 31, 35] have greatly improved multimodal
sual features to provide positional references at both levels,          reasoning and scene understanding in images [6, 8, 14, 37].
thereby enhancing the correspondence between textual rea-               However, existing LLMs/VLMs cannot directly process raw

Figure 2. Overview of the UZ3DVG framework with training and inference phases. In training, MSAG-RC converts RGB-D images into
spatial description pseudo-labels and reasoning chains to guide 3DVG model training, and RCD distills reasoning knowledge and logic
from a teacher network to a lightweight student network head. Reasoning-enhanced text features are aligned with 3D backbone features
(SpConv) and augmented via TSVDE, then processed by GeoSM to model global context and local geometry before the prediction head
outputs localization results. During inference, only point clouds and text inputs are used, without MSAG-RC and RCD-teacher.

view projection, and embodied-agent interaction.                                                                         Reasoning Chain Distillation (RCD). The spatial descrip-

inference, causing high latency and computational over-                                                                  ing the student network, while the Text-Semantic-guided
head. Our work aims to address these speed and deploy-                                                                   Visual Detail Enhancement (TSVDE) module samples and
ment challenges with UZ3DVG, which relies solely on 3D                                                                   augments details related to textual semantics from low-

dent network is designed to identify reasoning-relevant fea-                 ment module (TSVDE). During upsampling, the module

soning logic, and improve localization accuracy through a                    features to guide feature refinement. Specifically, it applies

Table 1. Evaluation of 3DVG methods on the ScanRefer [4] validation set. Results marked with †† are computed on a subset of 250 samples
(250/9508 ≈ 2.6%) from the validation set. Inference speed follows TSP3D [10] (batch size = 1, NVIDIA 3090 GPU). NR: Not Released.

 BUTD-DETR [15]           ECCV’22          Fully         82.88       64.98         44.73       33.97      50.42       38.60     3.33
 EDA [45]                 CVPR’23          Fully         85.76       68.57         49.13       37.64      54.59       42.26     3.34
